discovery: Electromagnetic metamaterials, negative refraction and transformation optics
motivation: Pendry showed that structured sub-wavelength 'atoms' (wire arrays, split-ring resonators) give engineered electric and magnetic responses. He predicted the perfect lens from negative refraction, and Smith carried out the first experimental demonstration of a negative-index medium. Pendry and Smith, and independently Leonhardt, then developed transformation optics: coordinate transformations of Maxwell's equations used as a design rule for the permittivity and permeability that steer light at will, which they used to demonstrate electromagnetic cloaking. Together these ideas turned the constitutive parameters of matter into design variables. They opened a field now spanning hyperbolic media, metasurfaces, flat optics, structured-light generation and coherently controlled resonances, and they reach from microwaves to visible light, acoustics and thermal transport. It is a transparent physical insight that became a universal control knob for light–matter interaction, used by experimentalists and engineers worldwide, including in India.
